To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hypoxia-activated Cre/LoxP switch vectors represent a promising approach for targeted gene therapy of cancer.
hypoxia-activated gene therapy vectors containing the Epo-HRE promoter and the Cre/loxP switch system, are effective in the treatment of human tumors in vitro and in vivo.
hypoxia-activated gene therapy of cancer may be optimized by the use of synthetic gene promoters and ‘molecular switches’.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel gene therapy approaches for the treatment of solid tumors.

the development of synthetic gene promoters that respond specifically to tumor hypoxia and radiation, and with the construction of ‘molecular switch vectors’ that enable sustained expression of the gene of interest.
the development of novel gene therapy vectors for the treatment of cancer and other diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study has shown that the HRE/CarG-switch is a promising strategy to target and effectively kill cancer cells.
the HRE/Cre/loxP system can be successfully applied for the treatment of hypoxic tumors.
hypoxia-activated gene therapy has the potential to be effective, but it is not yet ready for clinical use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HRE/CarG-switch is the first gene therapy approach that is activated by hypoxia and ionizing radiation, two factors that are present in the majority of solid tumors.
hypoxia and ionizing radiation are two important tumor characteristics that may be exploited to achieve selective gene therapy of cancer.

hypoxia-activated gene therapy vectors are more effective than vectors activated by radiation alone, and that the ‘molecular switch vector’ is more effective than the same inducibility system driving the gene of interest directly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hypoxia and radiation can be exploited as a double-edged sword for gene therapy of solid cancers.
we have shown that the use of hypoxia-responsive promoter elements can increase the efficacy of suicide gene therapy.
hypoxia-activated gene therapy is feasible.
